newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkey seeks medium-term samurai bond-minister.
newsitem.headline: Turkey seeks medium-term samurai bond-minister.

text.p: Turkish economy minister Gunes Taner said on Wednesday Turkey would seek a medium-term samurai bond issue as part of its plans for foreign borrowing.
"In the coming period we will go for a medium-term borrowing on the Japanese samurai markets," Taner said at a meeting of the Istanbul Chamber of Industry.

He did not provide any details of the plan. Turkish bond yields jumped around eight percentage points on Wednesday in response to remarks from Taner on Tuesday saying that inflation would probably hit 100 percent by the end of 1997.

But he said on Wednesday the three-week-old secularist government, made up of parties from the right and left, would seek to stick to its previous 85 percent target for inflation and would keep the lira exchange rate unchanged.
Taner also said the secularist coalition was preparing a programme to lower inflation.
"Inflation's trend is at such a stage that if we do not do anything, the uptrend ... will pose dangers," he said.
"We are preparing a program to change this trend."
